![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130823/assets/c46bf82e7609abe56e9e65ef0e81e21438a67e849d80d560baff5ab0c90bde11.png)

A plate with mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=x+2$, as shown above. Given that the region has an area of $\frac{9}{2},$ find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=2.$
question.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+2\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130823/assets/f48cd4e22c083d6c05ba9908a788402b05d839fea710a7328297d9e392e3636e.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=2$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-2|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{2M}{9}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}|x-2{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}(x-2)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(x-2)^{2}[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{-1}^{2}({x}^{2}-4x+4)(x+2-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{\int }_{-1}^{2}-{x}^{4}+5{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-4x+8\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}{[-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{5{x}^{4}}{4}-2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+8x]}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}[(-\frac{32}{5}+20-16-8+16)-(\frac{1}{5}+\frac{5}{4}+2-2-8)] \\  & =\frac{2M}{9}(\frac{28}{5}-(-\frac{131}{20})) \\  & =\frac{27M}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
